content: The safety and efficacy of vaccinations administered during or following treatment with atidarsagene autotemcel have not been studied. Vaccination is not recommended during the six weeks preceding the initiation of myeloablative conditioning and should be avoided until hematologic recovery is achieved following treatment. If possible, childhood vaccinations should be completed prior to the start of myeloablative conditioning. Live, non-replicating vaccines, such as smallpox (vaccinia) and monkeypox vaccines, should be avoided or alternative drugs should be considered. The same applies to other vaccines, including live varicella virus vaccine, live typhoid vaccine, yellow fever vaccine, and live zoster vaccine. Recombinant zoster vaccine and other vaccines, such as the tick-borne encephalitis vaccine, should also be avoided or replaced with alternatives. Antiretroviral (ART) medications, including tenofovir DF, tipranavir, zidovudine, abacavir, atazanavir, bictegravir, cabotegravir, dolutegravir, doravirine, efavirenz, and others, may interfere with the manufacturing process of atidarsagene autotemcel. ARTs should not be taken for at least one month before cell mobilization or for the expected duration required for the elimination of these medications. Vaccines such as the anthrax vaccine (adjuvanted or non-adjuvanted), cholera vaccine, chikungunya vaccine (live), dengue vaccine, and Ebola Zaire vaccine should also be avoided or replaced with alternatives. Similarly, COVID-19 vaccines, including adjuvanted (Novavax) and mRNA-based vaccines (Moderna and Pfizer), are not recommended during the specified period surrounding myeloablative conditioning and hematologic recovery. In all cases, the administration of childhood vaccinations before the initiation of myeloablative conditioning is advised if feasible.
